questions.prompt: Should the buyer accept off-site transformer manufacture on December 22, 2025 as the beginning of construction?
questions.context: The only physical work in 2025 is off-site manufacture of a custom main power transformer under a contract dated December 10, 2025. The independent engineer and the manufacturer describe that work, but the contract and production records have not been produced. If construction instead began with on-site piles on January 12, 2026, the domestic content threshold rises to 50%, so the 47.8% would fail and the credit rate would drop to 40%. The foreign entity material assistance rules would also apply, and no cost ratio has been prepared.

evidence.text: Under a binding written contract dated December 10, 2025, physical manufacture of the custom main power transformer began off site on December 22, 2025.
on-site physical work, beginning with pile installation for the tracker foundations, commenced on January 12, 2026.
No material assistance cost ratio calculation has been prepared because the restrictions do not apply to the Project.

options.label: Accept December 22, 2025 (off-site work substantiated)
options.consequence: Domestic content qualifies at the 45% threshold, and the foreign entity rules do not apply. The 50% credit rate holds.

options.label: Use on-site start of January 12, 2026
options.consequence: The 47.8% adjusted percentage fails the 50% threshold, so the domestic content bonus is lost. The rate drops to 40% and the credit falls by $14,200,000. The foreign entity rules apply and need a cost ratio before any credit can be relied on.

options.label: Defer until the contract and production records are produced
options.consequence: The start date, domestic content qualification and foreign entity applicability all stay open. Make delivery of the substantiating documents and the cost ratio a condition precedent.
